paper_metadata.title: Portfolio construction using a sampling-based variational quantum scheme

summary: The paper studies a gate-based sampling-based CVaR-VQA for bond ETF portfolio construction, reporting 31-qubit MPS simulations and 109-qubit IBM Heron hardware runs. The best reported post-processed hardware result is a 0.49% optimization gap for the TwoLocal bilinear ansatz, compared with 0.55% for TwoLocal color, 0.91% for BFCD color, and 0.39% in the simulator; classical CPLEX solves the 109-bond simplified instance to optimality in seconds. The paper does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage, and the classically hard regime is stated to be beyond 1,000 bonds.

experiments.description: 31-qubit MPS simulation study of sampling-based CVaR-VQA on a simplified portfolio-construction instance, used to tune CVaR alpha, circuit repetitions, and compare TwoLocal vs BFCD ansatzes.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: not reported; iterative optimization over epochs until convergence in reported experiments

hyperparameters.local_search: applied in some runs; for local-search results, only last 20 iterations processed

algorithm.parameter_initialization: all circuit parameters initialized to pi/3

optimizer_settings.parameter_bounds: parameters in [0, 2pi) as defined for V(theta)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: one qubit per bond/binary variable; simplified problem reduced to binary variables only
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x x^T Q x + 1^T max{0, s ⊙ (Ax - b)}; original portfolio objective minimizes squared deviations of portfolio metrics from targets with linear constraints
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: inequality constraints handled by non-slack penalty term 1^T max{0, s ⊙ (Ax - b)}; local-search post-processing used after sampling

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: BFCD with higher repetitions and alpha=0.1 gave better relative gaps; local search improved final solution quality

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper discusses potential quantum-classical advantages and better convergence for harder-to-simulate circuits, but does not demonstrate a proven speedup.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; paper states the original problem becomes classically hard beyond 1,000 bonds, but the reported experiment is only 31 qubits
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require scaling to the >1,000-bond regime with low-noise hardware and substantially more robust optimization
limiting_factors: Classical CPLEX is used as the benchmark and the paper does not show quantum superiority

Results depend on heuristic ansatz choice and local search
